If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The `appendOptionGroup` method in the `HelpFormatter` class appends an `OptionGroup` to the output buffer `buff`. If the `OptionGroup` is not required, it adds square brackets '[...]' to enclose the group.

Key points to note:
- It checks if the `OptionGroup` is required, and if not, adds '[' at the beginning and ']' at the end.
- It iterates over the options in the group, appending each option and handling the separator ' | ' between options.

This method seems to be crucial for handling the formatting of `OptionGroup` information in the output.

Next, I will provide a diagnosis based on the information gathered so far.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue reported describes an infinite loop in the wrapping code of `HelpFormatter` when the available space is insufficient to display a word on a single line, leading to a JVM crash with an OutOfMemoryError. 

Upon inspecting the implementation of key methods such as `printHelp`, `printUsage`, and `appendOptionGroup` in the `HelpFormatter` class, the way options and groups are processed and appended to the output buffer has been identified. The methods handle grouping, required options, and separators in the output formatting.

The issue may be related to the logic in the `appendOptionGroup` method when processing `OptionGroup` information and appending options with separators.

To further pinpoint the exact cause of the infinite loop leading to the OutOfMemoryError, additional analysis within the processing logic of `OptionGroup` and option grouping mechanisms may be necessary.

Considering the symptoms described in the issue report and the behavior of option grouping and formatting in `HelpFormatter`, the infinite loop issue appears to be connected to the way `OptionGroup` information is processed and displayed in the output.

Next steps would involve tracing the loop iteration and condition checking within the `OptionGroup` handling to identify the specific scenario causing the infinite loop.

Suggested methods for potential fixes:
- `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.appendOptionGroup(java.lang.StringBuffer, org.apache.commons.cli.OptionGroup)`
- `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printUsage(java.io.PrintWriter, int, java.lang.String, org.apache.commons.cli.Options)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
